title: Excel & Power Query
rows: Turn a range into an Excel Table.
Jump to / select to the edge of a data region.
Edit a cell / cycle reference anchors while editing a formula.
Insert today’s date / refresh all connections.
Open PivotTable options; press keys in sequence.
notes: Windows desktop shortcuts; laptop function keys may need Fn. Mac and web versions differ. XLOOKUP needs a supported Excel version.
Power Query routine: connect → preserve raw data → set types and UK date locale → trim/clean → investigate blanks and duplicates → merge/append → reconcile → load → refresh.
Merge adds columns by matching keys; append stacks rows. Check key uniqueness before a merge. Keep exception rows instead of silently deleting them.
Formula examples assume the named tables and columns exist. IFERROR is not a substitute for checking the denominator.

title: SQL & the T-SQL bridge
sub: Remember the pattern, then check the result.
rows: Choose columns / filter rows before grouping.
Aggregate by a defined grain / filter groups.
Keep every left-hand row; watch for one-to-many multiplication.
Test missing values / choose a deliberate replacement.
Name a CTE to make query stages readable.
Unique sequence / ties with gaps / ties without gaps.
Read a previous / next row within an ordered partition.
code:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT category, SUM(revenue) AS sales
  FROM sales
  WHERE sale_date >= '2026-01-01'
    AND sale_date < '2026-02-01'
  GROUP BY category
)
SELECT category, sales,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY sales DESC) AS sales_rank
FROM monthly;
notes: Logical order, simplified: FROM/JOIN → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → window calculations → SELECT → DISTINCT → ORDER BY → row limit. Write a CTE when you need to filter a window result.
T-SQL uses TOP (n) rather than PostgreSQL LIMIT n. Date functions, casts and identifier quoting vary; portable concepts do not make every query portable.
Use an explicit ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW frame for a row-by-row running total; order by a stable tie-breaker.
Before trusting a join: check key uniqueness, unmatched rows, row count and totals. Never use DISTINCT simply to conceal a broken join. Practise UPDATE/DELETE only in a safe copy.

title: Power BI, DAX & report operations
sub: Fast authoring is useful. Reliable measures matter more.
rows: Show available Power BI Desktop keyboard shortcuts.
Go to a line in the DAX formula bar.
Move a line in the DAX formula bar.
Group selected visuals; the same keys have a different formula-bar meaning.
code:
Revenue = SUM(Sales[Revenue])
Orders = DISTINCTCOUNT(Sales[OrderID])
Average Order Value = DIVIDE([Revenue], [Orders])
Revenue All Categories =
    CALCULATE([Revenue], REMOVEFILTERS(Products[Category]))
notes: Create these as measures; tables and columns are illustrative. A measure responds to filter context. A calculated column is evaluated row by row at refresh and stored.
Model first: define fact-table grain, use dimension keys, prefer one-to-many relationships and deliberate filter direction. Confirm the date table before time-intelligence work.
Release check: reconcile KPI totals → test slicers and blanks → add clear units/alt text → inspect mobile view → run Performance Analyzer → test RLS roles.

Service checklist: workspace access, gateway where needed, credentials, scheduled refresh, refresh-failure ownership and sharing permissions. Desktop success is not proof of Service refresh or security.

title: Statistics, metrics & data quality
sub: Keep the denominator, uncertainty and business question visible.
rows: Mean is sensitive to outliers; median is useful for skewed values.
SUM(value × weight) / SUM(weight); validate the weights.
(new − old) / old; format as a percentage and define what happens at old = 0.
30% − 20% = 10 percentage points; the relative increase is 50%.
Conversions / eligible opportunities over a defined period.
Q3 − Q1; inspect the distribution before using outlier rules.
Use STDEV.S for sample estimation; STDEV.P for the full population described.
Association is not evidence of causation.
code:
BEFORE ANALYSIS
Question → audience → metric → grain → period

AFTER EVERY TRANSFORMATION
Rows → keys → missingness → totals → exceptions

BEFORE SHARING
Source → assumptions → limits → privacy → owner
notes: A p-value is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true. Explain the test assumptions, effect size and uncertainty instead of treating 0.05 as an automatic business decision.
A frequentist 95% confidence procedure covers the fixed true parameter in 95% of repeated samples under its assumptions; it is not a guarantee about an individual outcome.
Missing is not automatically zero. Investigate causes and document any exclusion or imputation. Reconcile with an independent method where possible.
Use only permitted public/synthetic practice data. Minimise personal information, keep raw data unchanged and document transformations and retention.

title: Python, pandas & plotting
sub: Inspect first. Transform deliberately. Make the notebook reproducible.
rows: Preview rows / inspect types and missing counts.
Count missing values / exact duplicate rows.
Select explicit rows and columns; avoid chained assignment.
Parse dates; inspect new NaT values instead of ignoring them.
Order the result / export without the index.
code:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

sales = pd.read_csv("sales.csv")
products = pd.read_csv("products.csv")
out = sales.merge(products, on="product_id",
    how="left", validate="many_to_one", indicator=True)
assert len(out) == len(sales)
print(out["_merge"].value_counts())
summary = out.groupby("category", dropna=False)["revenue"].sum()
summary.sort_values().plot.barh()
plt.xlabel("Revenue (£)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("revenue_by_category.png", dpi=150)
notes: Example assumes the listed CSV columns exist and revenue is numeric. Resolve unmatched keys before interpreting category totals. Decide how missing revenue should be handled before summing.
Create a virtual environment; install required libraries and record versions. Restart the kernel and run every cell in order before sharing.
Python basics to recall: = assigns; == compares; indentation defines blocks; lists are ordered; dictionaries map keys to values. Use functions for repeated transformations.
Name chart units, period and source. Use bars for category comparisons, lines for time series and scatter plots for relationships.

title: Setup, Git & README essentials
sub: Keep the daily loop small and your public repository safe.
rows: Inspect changed files / inspect unstaged changes.
Stage a specific file / inspect what will be committed.
Update from the tracked remote; only use when you understand local history and conflicts.
Unstage a file without discarding the working copy.
Exclude credentials, private data, environments and generated files.
code:
git status
git diff
git add analysis.sql README.md
git diff --staged
git commit -m "Add validated monthly sales analysis"
git pull --rebase
git push

# README headings
# Question | Data | Method | Checks
# Findings | Limits | Reproduce | Sources
notes: Set up folders for raw data, cleaned data, SQL, notebooks, reports and screenshots. Power BI Desktop needs Windows access. Check Excel/Power Query version support before starting.
Do not use reset --hard, force push or history rewriting as a routine shortcut. Inspect files before staging; do not commit secrets or confidential data.
If a secret is exposed, revoke/rotate it immediately; deleting the latest file does not remove earlier Git history.
Add install/run steps, data source and licence, expected outputs and a screenshot. Check repository and demo links while logged out.

title: Projects, capstone & handover
sub: A repeatable workflow for every portfolio project.
rows: Write one useful question, its reader, the metric and success criteria.
Record source, licence, date, grain and limitations.
Check types, ranges, blanks, duplicate keys and suspicious values.
Keep raw inputs unchanged; document and reproduce each step.
Reconcile counts, joins and key totals independently.
Show three findings, an actionable recommendation and limits.
Package the workbook/query/report/notebook, README and screenshots.
Explain refresh, access, definitions, exceptions and who owns failures.
code:
CASE STUDY IN SIX LINES
Question: What decision does this support?
Data: Where did it come from and what does one row mean?
Method: What did I change or calculate?
Checks: How do I know the result is sound?
Finding: What changed, by how much, over which period?
Limit: What can this analysis not establish?
notes: Portfolio ladder: retail Excel → retail SQL → retail Power BI → public NHS pandas analysis → end-to-end regional capstone. Lead with your strongest three pieces.
Public healthcare projects need dataset definitions, reporting-period rules and published methodology. They do not prove experience with internal clinical systems.
Use screenshots, a PDF and a short demo if live sharing is unsuitable. Never use Publish to web for confidential or personal data.
Label synthetic work honestly. Describe what you built and verified; do not claim fictional savings, workplace deployment or business impact.

title: Revision, interviews & applications
sub: Short preparation routines—not shortcuts around understanding.
rows: 5 minutes explain → 10 minutes solve → 5 minutes check and log one gap.
Background → why analytics → evidence → role fit.
Question → data → method → validation → finding → limitation.
Situation → task → action → result; describe your own contribution.
Confirm grain and keys → write the query → test NULLs/ties → explain checks.
Verify location, level, essential skills, deadline and genuine paid employment.
Tool + question answered + checks + truthful result; link the project.
Role, employer, URL, closing date, fit, tailored evidence, status and follow-up.
code:
WEEKLY REVIEW
1. What can I now do without copying?
2. Which result have I independently checked?
3. What is the smallest remaining blocker?
4. Which role criteria can I demonstrate today?
5. What is my next repeatable practice session?
notes: Apply when you meet a role’s essential criteria; the roadmap week is not a ban on earlier applications. Excel-led reporting roles can have different requirements from SQL/BI roles.
Keep one main resource per tool. After a lesson, close it and reproduce the task on a different small dataset. Extend the calendar when needed rather than abandoning the habit.
Use truthful dates, responsibilities and results. A personal project is not employment experience and a certificate is not proof of independent delivery.
During an interview, clarify assumptions, explain uncertainty and say how you would verify an unfamiliar detail. Do not bluff or use unauthorised assistance.
